counterexample: x*y = 1 - y on {0,1} has the single cycle (0,0) -> (0,1) -> (1,1) -> (1,0) of length 4 = n^2 and is not a quasigroup; every n has full-period tables (Theorem 2); for n <= 4 none of them is a quasigroup (EXP-C16-01).
statement: As for Pisano periods (where (0, 0) is fixed), the maximal period of the pair map on an n-element magma is at most n^2 - 1, and the maximum is attained only by quasigroups.
title: H-C16-1: maximal period at most n^2 - 1, attained only by quasigroups (refuted)
